requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed appworker did not exist, then created it with useradd -m and verified uid=1000(appworker) gid=1000(appworker). Post-restart, getent passwd confirms the account persisted.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: A PAM limits.d config was written setting nofile and nproc soft/hard limits to 8192 and 256 respectively, and directly verified via a real login shell (su -l appworker) showing ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256. Re-verified identically after a full node restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and constraining its login sessions to 8192 open files / 256 processes — are directly and coherently satisfied by evidence: account creation confirmed via id/useradd, and limits confirmed via an actual login shell (su -l) ulimit check rather than just config inspection. The executor additionally ran the independent node-restart evidence protocol (not part of the public task contract), capturing a pre-restart boot_id, a deferred reboot with an ack returned before disconnection, a differing post-restart boot_id, and confirmed persistence of the account and limits afterward — a well-formed restart evidence trail. Operational hygiene is clean, with only a trivial /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the self-triggered reboot mechanism.
limitations: The task instruction does not specify restart or persistence as a requirement; the restart evidence is supplemental per the fixed protocol and does not affect scoring of the two material task outcomes, though it does strengthen confidence in persistence.

Login-session limit verification relied on `su -l` rather than a full independent login session (e.g., via SSH or a systemd user session with pam_limits applied through a display manager or cron), though su -l with a login shell is a standard and adequate way to exercise PAM limits.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were tightly scoped to the task (existence check, useradd, limits.d write, login-shell verification) plus the independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol (boot_id capture, deferred systemctl reboot, polling, post-restart re-verification). All state-changing actions have a clear purpose: account creation, limits configuration, or the mandatory restart evidence collection. The restart is a broad but well-bounded and fully-verified action with a clean before/after comparison showing recovered state (zero failed services, listening sockets equivalent modulo expected sshd/systemd PID changes from the reboot). The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a trivial byproduct of the self-scheduled reboot mechanism (cmd-8137ba31a3044cb5), which is negligible and not evidence of unwanted or unsafe change. No troubleshooting dead-ends, no unnecessary mutations, and no security-control weakening were observed.
